cases.input: I put my shoulder to the cellar stair door and try to force it.

arguments.narration:
Your Athletics check comes to 7 against a Hard DC of 14: failure.

The door does not give you an inch, and it tells you why: it is not a door that opens. The frame is set into stone at the top and the hinges are on the wrong side for a shoulder, and the whole thing was built by somebody who wanted a cellar to stay a cellar. You take your weight off it and the stair door sits there, unimpressed, with its little brass catch still holding. Nothing about it has changed.

arguments.narration:
You equip 1 brass whistle in the belt slot. The committed attribute changes from 12 to 14.

The whistle is heavier than it looks and colder, and it sits on your hip at the exact angle where you keep putting your hand when you are thinking. The locker door is still open. The stove has gone to coals and the watch room has that particular stillness it gets at the small hours, and somewhere below, the river lock turns over again for the third time since you sat down.
